turns.text: 2:08 pm update. can you make me a printable menu card for the fridge, with a grocery list layout? it's for my sunday batch cook, two dishes for the week: chili and baked pasta. judith just left for her condo at 5 so it's me and theo till monday, wait no, she leaves at 5, it's just 2 now, anyway she's leaving soon. i need this done before the witching hour starts and ruins the afternoon. please and thanks 🙃

Happy to. A few quick questions so the card is useful: do you want amounts for each dish, or just item names? And any ingredients you already have at home? If you'd rather not answer, I can make a clean first version now and you can tweak it.

item names plus rough amounts is great. also the list should be sorted for tomorrow's saturday trip to Ruiz Family Market, theo will be in the carrier so i want it fast, grouped by aisle/section. and note oat milk on it, i'm lactose intolerant. put it in table form if you can, i think better in tables

[Image: a one-page printable fridge card, portrait, titled "Sunday Batch Cook" with a soft green header. The top third is a two-column menu box: "Dish 1: Chili" and "Dish 2: Baked Pasta," each with a small checkbox for "cooked" and a line for notes. Below it is a grocery table with columns Section | Item | Amount | ✓.

Produce: onions (2), bell peppers (2), garlic (1 head), fresh basil (1 bunch)
Meat counter: ground beef or turkey (2 lb), Italian sausage (1 lb, optional for pasta)
Canned and dry: kidney beans (2 cans), black beans (1 can), crushed tomatoes (2 large cans), tomato paste (1 small can), pasta, rigatoni or penne (1 lb), chili powder, cumin
Dairy and alternatives: oat milk (1 carton, lactose intolerant, check label for no dairy), dairy-free mozzarella or shredded cheese alternative (1 bag)
Freezer or backup: foil trays (2) for storing portions

A bottom strip reads "Already at home?" with blank lines, and a footer note: "Oat milk, lactose-free cheese swap." Designed for letter paper, black and white friendly.]

I grouped it in the order of a typical store walk-through: produce, meat, canned and dry goods, then dairy alternatives, so you can go through it quickly. Since the Saturday trip is tomorrow, the sections are set up to tick off as you go. If you want, I can make a second version with a smaller footprint for your phone, or add fields for storing and reheating each dish.
this is perfect, printing it now. scoreboard: dad 1, witching hour 0 (so far). thanks!
Nice work, dad. Good luck with the shopping trip tomorrow and the cook on Sunday. If you want a reheating guide for the week's portions, just ask.
